edges.description: Impaired triglyceride hydrolysis causes cytoplasmic triglyceride droplet deposition in cardiomyocytes, coronary vascular smooth muscle cells, and skeletal muscle fibers.
Loss of ATGL-mediated lipolysis deprives cardiomyocytes and vascular smooth muscle cells of intracellularly mobilized long-chain fatty acids, causing cellular energy failure.
edges.target: Impaired Myocardial Long-Chain Fatty Acid Utilization and Energy Failure

edges.description: Cytoplasmic triacylglycerol droplet deposition in cardiac and skeletal muscle fibers manifests histologically as increased muscle lipid content.
Massive cardiomyocyte steatosis disrupts myocardial structure and contractility, producing severe cardiomyopathy.
Triglyceride accumulation in coronary vascular smooth muscle cells drives diffuse concentric coronary arterial wall thickening and stenosis.
Concomitant neutral lipid storage in skeletal muscle fibers produces skeletal myopathy.
Cardiomyocyte bioenergetic failure directly impairs ventricular systolic and diastolic performance.
edges.source: Impaired Myocardial Long-Chain Fatty Acid Utilization and Energy Failure

edges.description: Myocardial steatosis and bioenergetic failure create an arrhythmogenic substrate for ventricular arrhythmias.
edges.source: Impaired Myocardial Long-Chain Fatty Acid Utilization and Energy Failure

edges.description: Diffuse concentric triglyceride-deposit coronary stenosis manifests clinically as treatment-refractory coronary artery disease.
Low-output congestive heart failure produces exertional and resting dyspnea.
Lipid-storage cardiomyopathy progresses to intractable adult-onset low-output congestive heart failure.
Diffuse concentric coronary artery atherosclerosis causes resting and stress-related chest pressure and angina pectoris.
Lipid-storage skeletal myopathy causes myofiber injury and elevated serum creatine kinase activity.
Cardiac arrhythmias manifest clinically with palpitations.

nodes.description: Biallelic PNPLA2 variants reduce adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL) catalytic activity on cytoplasmic lipid droplets, impairing the rate-limiting intracellular hydrolysis of triacylglycerol to release long-chain fatty acids as a major myocardial energy substrate.

evidence.reference_title: Triglyceride deposit cardiomyovasculopathy: a rare cardiovascular disorder.
evidence.snippet:
Triglyceride deposit cardiomyovasculopathy (TGCV) is a phenotype primarily
reported in patients carrying genetic mutations in PNPLA2 encoding adipose
triglyceride lipase (ATGL) which releases long chain fatty acid (LCFA) as a
major energy source by the intracellular TG hydrolysis.
